title: Posterior and epsilon-parameterized mean
goal:
Implement two functions from Sections 2 and 3.2.

`posterior_mean_var(x_t, x0, t, betas, alpha_bars)` returns the mean $\tilde\mu_t(x_t, x_0)$ and variance $\tilde\beta_t$ of $q(x_{t-1} | x_t, x_0)$ (Equations 6 and 7). Use $\bar\alpha_0 = 1$, so that at $t = 1$ the variance is 0 and the mean is $x_0$.

`mean_from_eps(x_t, eps_pred, t, betas, alpha_bars)` returns $\mu_\theta(x_t, t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}\left(x_t - \frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\epsilon_\theta\right)$ (Equation 11).

`t` is a single integer from 1 to `T`. The starter includes finished `make_schedule` and `q_sample` helpers.
hints: For $\bar\alpha_{t-1}$ don't write `alpha_bars[t - 2]`. At `t = 1` that index is `-1`, which silently reads $\bar\alpha_T$. Branch on `t == 1` and use 1.0.
To check yourself, build $x_t$ with `q_sample` from a known $\epsilon$. Then `mean_from_eps(x_t, eps, ...)` must equal `posterior_mean_var(x_t, x0, ...)[0]`.
